2016.emphasis_summary: The excerpts stress board diversity and sustainability leadership, citing that 50% of independent directors are women or minorities and an 11th consecutive year of Dow Jones Sustainability index inclusion.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: The 2017 excerpts repeat the 50% women-or-minority independent-director statistic and add product-excellence messaging plus 2014-2015 investments in new product development, manufacturing and supply chain.
2017.notable_shifts: Relative to 2016 the emphasis shifts from sustainability-index recognition toward product quality and manufacturing investment, while the board-diversity statistic is repeated.

2018.emphasis_summary: The excerpts now lead with a standalone SUSTAINABILITY section framing Abbott as a responsible and sustainable business that helps people live fuller, healthier lives, alongside Product Excellence language.
2018.notable_shifts: The 2018 filing adds the standalone sustainability section and populates human-capital text for the first time (it was empty in 2016 and 2017), though that text is largely auditor-ratification language, which suggests the extraction picked up adjacent content.

2019.emphasis_summary: Corporate responsibility is the lead theme, framed as Corporate Responsibility and Stewardship with commitments to environmental impact and ethical business, a diverse global footprint with redundancies, and supplier risk evaluation.
2019.notable_shifts: The 2018 sustainability wording is re-labeled as Corporate Responsibility and Stewardship, and the excerpt adds supplier-selection and risk-evaluation language and a dedicated senior-management role with regular Board updates.

2020.emphasis_summary: Sustainability governance leads, with a roadmap focused on the most relevant industry and company-specific risks and opportunities, alongside compensation text that separates long-term incentive decisions (performance through 2018) from annual incentive payouts.
2020.notable_shifts: The sustainability section becomes more formal, framed around material risks and opportunities, and the human-capital excerpt returns after being empty in 2019.

2021.emphasis_summary: The 2030 Sustainability Plan launch leads, framed around new life-changing technologies, affordability and access, and breaking down barriers, with a pandemic-era narrative on maintaining access to essential products.
2021.notable_shifts: COVID-19 becomes a heavy theme (about 20 hits, up from none), the 2030 Sustainability Plan replaces the 2020 general roadmap wording, and the Board topics expand to include sustainability reporting.

2022.emphasis_summary: The excerpts combine the 2030 Sustainability Plan with COVID-19 testing leadership, an innovation-pipeline message, and a commitment to expand affordable access to care for underserved, diverse and at-risk communities.
2022.notable_shifts: Versus 2021 the excerpts add concrete climate targets (a 30% cut in absolute Scope 1 and 2 carbon emissions from a 2018 baseline) and a fuller board risk-oversight narrative (risk-keyword hits rise from about 6 to about 31), including cybersecurity and data protection.

2023.emphasis_summary: Climate leads, framed as Build a Foundation for the Future with support for the Science Based Targets initiative and reductions in Scope 1, 2 and 3 carbon emissions, alongside a Board refreshment section.
2023.notable_shifts: The 2023 text extends the 2022 Scope 1 and 2 target to Scope 3 and adds SBTi support, and it introduces board-composition and refreshment language (six new independent director nominees since 2018, three women and three minorities).

2024.emphasis_summary: Shareholder value leads, with five-year total shareholder return above the peer median credited to strong sustainable performance, and a governance section on board refreshment (six new independent directors since 2018, three women and three minorities).
2024.notable_shifts: The 2024 excerpts shift from the 2023 climate and SBTi framing to a TSR and performance narrative, while the board-refreshment statement is repeated nearly verbatim.
